analyzed_vuln.description: Double-free is caused by parse_aliasf storing duplicate ownership pointers in aliasf when decode_flags() returns the same heap pointer for malformed numeric FLAG aliases. In FLAG_NUM mode, an entry like "AF -25" is parsed by decode_flags as len=1 with value 0xFFE7 (unsigned cast of negative), and parse_aliasf sorts/stores that pointer without validating negativity or canonicalizing ownership. Later, HashMgr::free_table() frees ptr->astr via free_flag() for dictionary entries using that alias (because TESTAFF(..., ONLYUPCASEFLAG, alen) can be true for this malformed value), and then HashMgr::~HashMgr() unconditionally delete[]s all aliasf entries, freeing the same allocation again.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger via affdicfuzzer with an affix file using "FLAG num" and AF alias table entries containing negative numeric flags (e.g., "AF -25") plus alias references in dictionary words (e.g., "/1"). Data flow: load_config()->parse_aliasf()->decode_flags allocates alias flag arrays and stores them in aliasf; load_tables()/add_word attaches alias pointers to hentry::astr; on destruction free_table() may free alias-owned astr, then destructor frees aliasf again, causing double-free.
